title: AI / Machine Learning Engineer Readiness
description: Evaluate your expertise in neural network architectures, backpropagation, Transformers, LLMs, RAG pipelines, and model deployment.

questions.question: What is the primary role of the activation function (e.g., ReLU, GELU) in a deep neural network?
options: To introduce non-linearity, allowing the network to learn arbitrary complex functions beyond linear combinations
To normalize input feature vectors to unit length
To compute matrix multiplication on the GPU
To prevent gradient updates in the input layer
questions.explanation: Without non-linear activations, stacking multiple dense layers collapses mathematically into a single equivalent linear transformation.

questions.question: What mechanism enables Transformer architectures to process input sequence tokens in parallel rather than sequentially like RNNs?
options: Multi-Head Self-Attention and Positional Encodings
Recurrent Hidden State Vectors
Long Short-Term Memory Gating Units
Convolutional Pooling Layers
questions.explanation: Self-attention computes attention weights between all token pairs concurrently, while positional encodings inject sequence order information.

questions.question: What does RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) do in modern LLM applications?
options: Retrieves relevant external domain documents via semantic search and injects them into the LLM prompt context before generation
Retrains model weights from scratch every time a user asks a question
Converts text prompts into 3D animations
Encrypts LLM token streams using symmetric cryptography
questions.explanation: RAG enhances LLM outputs with accurate, up-to-date facts retrieved dynamically from vector databases, reducing hallucinations.

questions.question: What is the purpose of LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) in parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT)?
options: Freezes the pre-trained weights and injects trainable rank-decomposition matrices into transformer layers, vastly reducing memory
Quantizes all weights to 1-bit binary representations
Removes half of the transformer attention heads permanently
Increases the context window by compression
questions.explanation: LoRA decomposes weight update matrices $\Delta W$ into low-rank matrices $A \times B$, updating <1% of parameters while preserving performance.

questions.question: Which loss function is standard for training multi-class classification neural networks with Softmax output?
options: Categorical Cross-Entropy Loss
Mean Squared Error (MSE)
Mean Absolute Error (MAE)
Hinge Loss
questions.explanation: Categorical Cross-Entropy calculates the divergence between predicted probability distributions (from Softmax) and one-hot ground-truth labels.

questions.question: What is the 'Vanishing Gradient Problem' during deep neural network backpropagation?
options: Gradients become exponentially small as they propagate backward through layers, stopping early weights from updating
The model loss becomes zero after one epoch
Learning rate automatically decays to infinity
Weights overflow 32-bit floating point boundaries
questions.explanation: With functions like Sigmoid or Tanh, derivative values < 1 multiplied through many layers cause gradient signals to vanish to near-zero.

questions.question: In Vector Databases (such as Pinecone, Chroma, Milvus), what metric measures the cosine of the angle between two embedding vectors?
options: Cosine Similarity
Euclidean Distance (L2)
Manhattan Distance (L1)
Hamming Distance
questions.explanation: Cosine similarity measures vector direction similarity independent of magnitude, producing values between -1 and 1.

questions.question: What is the key advantage of PyTorch over older static computation graph frameworks?
options: Dynamic computation graphs (Define-by-Run) allowing runtime graph changes and seamless Python debugging
It only runs on quantum computers
It eliminates the need for GPU accelerators
It has no support for tensor autograd
questions.explanation: PyTorch constructs computational graphs dynamically on each forward pass, making custom architectures and native Python debugging straightforward.

questions.question: What is 'Temperature' in LLM token generation sampling?
options: A hyperparameter scaling logits to control randomness: lower values yield deterministic outputs; higher values yield creative variety
The physical temperature of the GPU hardware
The number of GPUs allocated to inference
The token generation rate per second
questions.explanation: Dividing logits by temperature before softmax flattens (high T) or sharpens (low T) the probability distribution.

questions.question: What is the primary function of MLOps tools like MLflow or Weights & Biases?
options: Tracking experiments, logging hyperparameters, versioning models, and managing the model registry
Generating synthetic training images
Writing Python unit tests automatically
Serving HTML frontend templates
questions.explanation: MLOps platforms track experiments across runs, log metrics/artifacts, and provide model registries for deployment governance.
